newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ross says wall slip to cut 1996/97 output.
newsitem.headline: Ross says wall slip to cut 1996/97 output.

text.p: Ross Mining NL said on Tuesday it was revising down its forecast gold yield for 1996/97 (July/June) by 10,000 ounces to 77,000 ounces due to a major pit wall slip at its Glen Eva satellite pit near the Yandon gold mine in central Queensland.

"The slip means that access to a large tonnage of broken, high-grade ore (five grammes of gold per tonne) in the Stage 1 pit, is temporarily restricted, but the ore will be fully recoverable in the next quarter," Ross said in a statement.
Employees were not endangered due to an early warning system.

As a result of the wall slip, gold production for the current quarter will be reduced by 10,000 ounces and, consequently, gold production for the financial year is forecast to be about 77,000 ounces, Ross said.
"The outcome of this temporary setback will be that gold output from our Queensland operations will be boosted to a newly-scheduled 100,000 ounces of fine gold for the 1997/98 financial year."
Ross said the company's overall gold hedging position has been restructured in such a way that 100,000 ounces can be delivered at a gold price of A$550 per ounce in the 1997/98 financial year.
Ross shares were trading five cents lower at 95 each cents at 11.33 a.m. (0133 GMT).
